match.reason: No bank point teaches a business's compliance duties to lodge returns, pay company tax, collect GST and withhold wage tax on time; the closest cards cover tax incidence, tax reform goals, company tax as a finance factor, or individual net pay calculations, which are different ideas.

draft.title: Tax compliance
card: Tax compliance means meeting a business's tax duties, on time. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) collects most of these taxes.
Income tax
A business lodges a return each year and pays tax on its profit. A company pays company tax. A sole trader pays income tax on the profit as part of their own return.
GST
A business registered for GST adds it to its prices, collects it from customers and passes it on to the ATO.
PAYG withholding
An employer takes tax out of each worker's wages and sends it to the ATO. The worker's pay is the amount after this tax is taken out.
draft.remember: Lodge returns, pay income or company tax, collect GST and withhold tax from wages, all on time.

a.q: Mei runs a registered café with two employees. Each pay day she takes tax out of their wages and sends it to the ATO. What is this duty called?
opts: PAYG withholding
GST collection
Company tax
Lodging a return
a.why: Taking tax out of wages and sending it to the ATO is PAYG withholding. GST is the tax added to prices, so it is the tempting wrong answer, but it is collected from customers, not taken from wages.
a.clue: Whose money is the tax taken from?

b.q: Luca's registered plumbing business charges customers GST on every job. He keeps the GST in his bank account and spends it on a new van. What has Luca done wrong?
opts: Kept GST that he should have passed on to the ATO
Charged GST, which only employees can pay
Paid company tax on his profit twice
Taken tax out of his own wages
b.why: A business registered for GST collects it on behalf of the ATO and must pass it on. It is not the business's own income. Income tax is a different duty, on the profit.
b.clue: Who does the GST money really belong to?

b.best: Kept GST that he should have passed on to the ATO

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest (11 words against 7 for each of the others). It is also the only one that restates the stem's situation, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

The stem says Luca keeps the GST in his account and spends it on a van, but never says he fails to pay it to the ATO when it is due. A business can use the cash before its BAS is due, so the stem should state plainly that he never passes it on.

check.summary: The facts are sound and both answers are clear. In question b the right option stands out as the longest, and the stem should state outright that Luca never pays the GST to the ATO.
